h3. Problem

MDR's [config/rbac/external_remediation_clusterrole.yaml|https://github.com/medik8s/machine-deletion-remediation/blob/main/config/rbac/external_remediation_clusterrole.yaml] uses {{machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}} as the raw ClusterRole name. The other three remediators (FAR, SNR, SBR) all use the bare name {{ext-remediation}} and rely on the kustomize {{namePrefix}} to produce the final deployed name.

Because MDR already bakes the project name into the raw YAML, kustomize prepends the prefix *again*, producing a double-prefix on the cluster:

{{machine-deletion-remediation-machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}}

h3. Why this matters

* *Tooling must special-case MDR.* Any script or automation that constructs ClusterRole names programmatically (e.g. {{<operator>-ext-remediation}}) works for FAR, SNR, and SBR but silently misses MDR. Found during review of [dragonfly/tools MR !285|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/dragonfly/tools/-/merge_requests/285], where the cleanup script had to hardcode the double-prefix name.
* *Future namePrefix changes break unpredictably.* If MDR's namePrefix is ever updated (as SBR did when it changed from {{storage-based-remediation-}} to {{sbr-operator-}}), the double-prefix would change in a non-obvious way, breaking any downstream tooling that references the old name.
* *Inconsistency across remediators.* All four remediators serve the same role (providing an ext-remediation ClusterRole for NHC aggregation), but MDR's naming breaks the uniform pattern, making the RBAC model harder to reason about.

h3. Fix

* Rename the raw ClusterRole name in {{config/rbac/external_remediation_clusterrole.yaml}} from {{machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}} to {{ext-remediation}}.
* Regenerate the bundle ({{make bundle}}).
* The deployed ClusterRole name becomes {{machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}} (single prefix) — matching the pattern of the other remediators.

{{machine-deletion-remediation-machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}}

h3. Why this matters

* *Tooling must special-case MDR.* Any script or automation that constructs ClusterRole names programmatically (e.g. {{<operator>-ext-remediation}}) works for FAR, SNR, and SBR but silently misses MDR. Found during review of [dragonfly/tools MR !285|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/dragonfly/tools/-/merge_requests/285], where the cleanup script had to hardcode the double-prefix name.
* *Future namePrefix changes break unpredictably.* If MDR's namePrefix is ever updated (as SBR did when it changed from {{storage-based-remediation-}} to {{sbr-operator-}}), the double-prefix would change in a non-obvious way, breaking any downstream tooling that references the old name.
* *Inconsistency across remediators.* All four remediators serve the same role (providing an ext-remediation ClusterRole for NHC aggregation), but MDR's naming breaks the uniform pattern, making the RBAC model harder to reason about.

h3. Upgrade risk analysis

Renaming the raw ClusterRole changes the deployed name on the cluster. This is *functionally safe* but creates an orphaned resource on upgrade.

*No functional risk.* NHC discovers remediators via the aggregation label {{rbac.ext-remediation/aggregate-to-ext-remediation: "true"}}, not by ClusterRole name. The aggregation controller ([aggregation.go|https://github.com/medik8s/node-healthcheck-operator/blob/main/internal/controller/rbac/aggregation.go]) creates a parent {{node-healthcheck-operator-aggregation}} ClusterRole with a label-selector AggregationRule. No ClusterRoleBinding references the ext-remediation ClusterRole by name. Renaming it does not break remediation discovery.

*Orphaned ClusterRole on upgrade.* The rename changes the deployed name from {{machine-deletion-remediation-machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}} to {{machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}}. On upgrade:

* *OLM v0:* creates the new-named ClusterRole via InstallPlan; the old-named one is not tracked for cleanup and stays on the cluster indefinitely.
* *OLM v1:* operator-controller owns the new name; the old one is unowned and orphaned.
* *OCP upgrades:* same OLM behavior applies — the orphan persists across OCP versions.

The orphan still carries the aggregation label, so NHC aggregates duplicate rules (same permissions twice). This is functionally harmless but creates clutter.

h3. Fix

# Rename the raw ClusterRole name in {{config/rbac/external_remediation_clusterrole.yaml}} from {{machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}} to {{ext-remediation}}.
# Regenerate the bundle ({{make bundle}}). The deployed name becomes {{machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}} (single prefix) — matching the pattern of the other remediators.
# Add a one-time startup migration in the MDR operator to delete the old ClusterRole {{machine-deletion-remediation-machine-deletion-remediation-ext-remediation}} if it exists. This handles the upgrade path for both OLM v0 and OLM v1.

h2. Background

Medik8s operators use inconsistent pod labeling. 5 of 6 operators use the legacy kubebuilder label {{control-plane=controller-manager}} while NHC follows K8s community recommendations ({{app.kubernetes.io/*}}). This inconsistency was surfaced during PR#21 testing (shared dev environment) where dev targets that use label selectors fail to find NHC pods.

Related: [RHWA-449|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHWA-449] (Telco best practices evaluation)

h2. Current State

||*Operator*||*Deployment Selector*||*Additional Pod Labels*||*Scheme*||
|*NHC*|{{app.kubernetes.io/component=controller-manager}}|{{app.kubernetes.io/name=node-healthcheck-operator}}|Modern (K8s recommended)|
|*SNR*|{{control-plane=controller-manager}}|{{self-node-remediation-operator=""}} (commonLabels)|Legacy kubebuilder|
|*FAR*|{{control-plane=controller-manager}}|{{app.kubernetes.io/name=fence-agents-remediation-operator}} (commonLabels)|Hybrid|
|*MDR*|{{control-plane=controller-manager}}|(none, no unique label)|Legacy, no uniqueness|
|*NMO*|{{control-plane=controller-manager}}|{{node-maintenance-operator=""}} (commonLabels)|Legacy kubebuilder|
|*SBR*|{{control-plane=controller-manager}}|{{app.kubernetes.io/name=sbr-operator}} (commonLabels)|Hybrid|

h2. K8s Community Recommendation

From [K8s Common Labels|https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/common-labels/] the {{app.kubernetes.io/*}} prefix is recommended:

||*Label*||*Purpose*||*Example*||
|{{app.kubernetes.io/name}}|Application name|{{self-node-remediation}}|
|{{app.kubernetes.io/instance}}|Unique instance|{{self-node-remediation-xyz}}|
|{{app.kubernetes.io/version}}|Version (never in selectors)|{{0.20.0}}|
|{{app.kubernetes.io/component}}|Component role|{{controller}}|
|{{app.kubernetes.io/part-of}}|Higher-level app|{{medik8s}}|
|{{app.kubernetes.io/managed-by}}|Managing tool|{{kustomize}}|

h2. Comparison with Standard Operators

||*Operator*||*Uses app.kubernetes.io/**||*Selector*||
|*cert-manager*|Yes (full)|{{name}} + {{instance}} + {{component}}|
|*prometheus-operator*|Yes (full)|{{name}} + {{component}}|
|*ArgoCD*|Yes (full)|{{name}} only|
|*Istio*|Partial (pods, not selector)|{{istio: pilot}} (legacy)|
|*OLM*|No|{{app: olm-operator}}|
|*OpenShift built-in*|No (use {{k8s-app}} or {{app}})|Single label per operator|

The broader K8s ecosystem (cert-manager, prometheus-operator, ArgoCD) standardized on {{app.kubernetes.io/*}}. NHC already follows this. OpenShift built-in operators do not, but they use unique labels (not shared {{control-plane=controller-manager}}).

h2. Problems with Current State

# *Non-unique selectors*: 5 operators share {{control-plane=controller-manager}}. If deployed in the same namespace, their selectors would collide. MDR has zero distinguishing labels.
# *Tooling incompatibility*: Any tool using label selectors to find operator pods must handle both conventions or miss NHC.
# *Certsuite test coverage*: The Red Hat best practices certsuite tests may validate label usage patterns.

h2. Risks of Changing Labels

* *Deployment selector immutability (CRITICAL)*: {{spec.selector.matchLabels}} is immutable in {{apps/v1}}. Cannot be changed on a running deployment.
* *OLM upgrade behavior (CRITICAL)*: If {{matchLabels}} change between CSV versions, OLM enters an infinite retry loop (known issues: OLM #952, #1608, #2748). Workaround: use a different Deployment name in the new CSV.
* *Service endpoints*: If pod labels change, pods silently drop out of Service EndpointSlice.
* *NetworkPolicies*: Pod label change can silently remove network isolation.
* *PodDisruptionBudgets*: Pod loses disruption protection.
* *Monitoring*: ServiceMonitors and PodMonitors may lose targets.

h2. Safe Migration Path

# Use a different Deployment name in the new CSV version. OLM creates fresh Deployment, garbage-collects old one.
# Update Service selectors, NetworkPolicies, PDBs, and PodMonitors simultaneously.
# Verify monitoring post-change.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

# Decide target label scheme for all Medik8s operators (recommend {{app.kubernetes.io/*}} per K8s community)
# Document migration plan per operator considering OLM upgrade safety
# Track per-operator implementation in sub-tasks

| {{app.kubernetes.io/managed\-by}} | Managing tool | {{kustomize}} |

h2. Comparison with Standard Operators

|| Operator || Uses app.kubernetes.io/\* || Selector ||
| _cert\-manager_ | Yes \(full\) | {{name}} \+ {{instance}} \+ {{component}} |
| _prometheus\-operator_ | Yes \(full\) | {{name}} \+ {{component}} |
| _ArgoCD_ | Yes \(full\) | {{name}} only |
| _Istio_ | Partial \(pods, not selector\) | {{istio: pilot}} \(legacy\) |
| _OLM_ | No | {{app: olm\-operator}} |
| _OpenShift built\-in_ | No \(use {{k8s\-app}} or {{app}}\) | Single label per operator |

Conclusion: The broader K8s ecosystem \(cert\-manager, prometheus\-operator, ArgoCD\) standardized on {{app.kubernetes.io/\*}}. NHC already follows this. OpenShift built\-in operators do not, but they use unique labels \(not shared {{control\-plane=controller\-manager}}\).

h2. Problems with Current State

h1. _Non\-unique selectors_: 5 operators share {{control\-plane=controller\-manager}} \- if deployed in the same namespace, their selectors would collide. MDR has zero distinguishing labels.
h1. _Tooling incompatibility_: Any tool using label selectors to find operator pods must handle both conventions or miss NHC.
h1. _Certsuite test coverage_: The Red Hat best practices certsuite tests may validate label usage patterns.
h2. Risks of Changing Labels

* _Deployment selector immutability \(CRITICAL\)_: {{spec.selector.matchLabels}} is immutable in {{apps/v1}}. Cannot be changed on a running deployment.
* _OLM upgrade behavior \(CRITICAL\)_: If {{matchLabels}} change between CSV versions, OLM enters an infinite retry loop \(known issues: OLM #952, #1608, #2748\). Workaround: use a different Deployment name in the new CSV.
* _Service endpoints_: If pod labels change, pods silently drop out of Service EndpointSlice.
* _NetworkPolicies_: Pod label change can silently remove network isolation.
* _PodDisruptionBudgets_: Pod loses disruption protection.
* _Monitoring_: ServiceMonitors/PodMonitors may lose targets.

h2. Safe Migration Path

h1. Use a different Deployment name in the new CSV version \- OLM creates fresh Deployment, garbage\-collects old one
h1. Update Service selectors, NetworkPolicies, PDBs, and PodMonitors simultaneously
h1. Verify monitoring post\-change
h2. Acceptance Criteria

h1. Decide target label scheme for all Medik8s operators \(recommend {{app.kubernetes.io/\*}} per K8s community\)
h1. Document migration plan per operator considering OLM upgrade safety
h1. Track per\-operator implementation in sub\-tasks

items.fromString:
Root cause identified and fix pushed to PR [https://github.com/medik8s/self\-node\-remediation/pull/315|https://github.com/medik8s/self-node-remediation/pull/315]

After SysRq hard reboot, the container runtime overlay storage can get corrupted \(CreateContainerError: readlink /var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/l: invalid argument\). This prevents the e2e helper pod from starting on the rebooted worker node, causing all reboot\-detection tests to time out.

The fix replaces helper pod\-based boot time detection with Kubernetes Node API bootID \(node.status.nodeInfo.bootID\). Boot ID is a kernel\-generated UUID that changes on every reboot \-\- no pods, no image pulls, no exec needed.

CI results after the fix: all e2e tests pass on OCP 4.22, 4.23, and 5.0 \(15/15 checks green\).

Further analysis of the OCP 5.0 e2e run on PR #315 revealed the /proc/stat fix alone is insufficient. The worker node events prove it does reboot successfully \(NodeReboot at 14:34 \-> NodeReady at 14:38, \~4 minutes\), but the helper pod cannot start on the rebooted node.

Root cause: the helper pod uses ubi9/ubi:latest which defaults ImagePullPolicy to Always. After node reboot, OVN/SDN pods need time to initialize before external network works. During this window, image pulls to registry.access.redhat.com fail and the helper pod stays in ErrImagePull. The podReadyTimeout of 2 minutes was insufficient.

Added a second commit to PR #315 with:
\- ImagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent on helper pod \(use cached image after reboot\)
\- podReadyTimeout increased from 2 to 5 minutes
\- nodeExecTimeout increased from 5 to 10 minutes
\- Diagnostic logging \(pod phase/conditions/containerStatuses\) when helper pod fails to start

Note: the 4.22 and 4.23 failures on PR #315 were unrelated CI infrastructure issues \(cluster install failure and release payload pod scheduling respectively\). Only the 5.0 run actually executed the e2e tests.

Retesting all 3 OCP versions now.

Failure chain:
  Kernel 6.12 volatile mount change
  \-> CRI\-O overlay storage corrupts after SysRq hard reboot
  \-> New pods fail: CreateContainerError: readlink overlay/l: invalid argument
  \-> E2e helper pod \(reads boot time\) cannot start on rebooted worker node
  \-> Reboot detection times out \(boot time = zero value\)
  \-> 5/6 e2e specs cascade\-fail \(control plane test passes — overlay recovers faster on masters\)

Likely trigger: Kernel 6.12.80 \(April 2026\) changed overlayfs volatile mount handling:
[https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/commit/?id=6c0cfbe020c0|https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/commit/?id=6c0cfbe020c0]
CRI\-O uses volatile mounts for every container.
containerd hit the same regression and fixed it in April 2026:
[https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/13250|https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/13250]
[https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13256|https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13256]
OCP 5.0 \(RHEL 10, kernel 6.12\) likely picked this up via errata in early June.
Known related issues in containers/storage:
[https://github.com/containers/storage/issues/1064|https://github.com/containers/storage/issues/1064]
[https://github.com/containers/storage/issues/1136|https://github.com/containers/storage/issues/1136]

Fix: [https://github.com/medik8s/self\-node\-remediation/pull/315|https://github.com/medik8s/self-node-remediation/pull/315]
Replaced helper pod with Node API bootID \(node.status.nodeInfo.bootID\) — no pods, no image pulls, no overlay storage dependency. 15/15 CI jobs passing \(4.22, 4.23, 5.0 e2e all green\).

Root cause identified and fix PR opened: [https://github.com/medik8s/self\-node\-remediation/pull/315|https://github.com/medik8s/self-node-remediation/pull/315]

The e2e helper pod used dnf install procps to get boot time, which fails silently when Red Hat package repos are unreachable from CI cluster nodes. Replaced with reading /proc/stat btime field \(no package installation needed\). Also added error logging in CheckReboot and helper pod cleanup.

h2. Problem

Since June 2026, all open SNR PRs experience identical e2e test failures across OCP 4.22, 4.23, and 5.0. The failure pattern is consistent regardless of the PR's code changes, pointing to a CI infrastructure issue rather than code regressions.

5 of 6 e2e specs fail on every failing run. The only passing test is the Control Plane Remediation \(Resource Deletion Strategy\) targeting a master node.

h2. Failure Pattern

The root failure is in worker node remediation: the SNR operator triggers remediation but the worker node never reboots \(or the reboot is never detected\). The privileged helper pod that checks boot time returns Go's zero value \(0001\-01\-01T00:00:00Z\) after \~660 seconds, indicating it could never read the boot time from the target node post\-remediation.

After the first worker test fails, it leaves the node in a degraded/unreachable state, causing all 4 subsequent worker\-targeted specs to cascade\-fail in BeforeEach with: "Timed out after 300s. Could not get boot time on target node". The helper pod keeps being recreated every \~2.5 minutes but never succeeds.

An additional infra issue is observed: the src\-bundle step intermittently fails with "no image found in manifest list for architecture arm64" \(retries and succeeds\).

h2. OCP Version Failure Matrix

Failure rates: OCP 4.22 \-\- 3/4 PRs \(75%\), OCP 4.23 \-\- 2/4 PRs \(50%\), OCP 5.0 \-\- 3/3 PRs \(100%\).

||PR||Description||4.22||4.23||5.0||
|#314|Bump golang.org/x/net|pending|pending|pending|
|#311|Catalog multi\-channel support|FAIL|PASS|FAIL|
|#310|Node\-scoped caching \(RHWA\-1026\)|PASS|FAIL|not run|
|#309|readOnlyRootFilesystem on DaemonSet|FAIL|FAIL|FAIL|
|#308|Runner image ubuntu\-24.04|FAIL|PASS|FAIL|

h2. Example Failure \(PR 308, OCP 4.22\)

Prow job: [https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test\-platform\-results/pr\-logs/pull/medik8s\_self\-node\-remediation/308/pull\-ci\-medik8s\-self\-node\-remediation\-main\-4.22\-openshift\-e2e/2072418710940815360|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/pr-logs/pull/medik8s_self-node-remediation/308/pull-ci-medik8s-self-node-remediation-main-4.22-openshift-e2e/2072418710940815360]

Root cause \-\- worker node reboot never detected \(test 1 of 6\):
{code}
\[FAILED\] Timed out after 660.135s.
Expected
    : 0001\-01\-01T00:00:00Z
to be >
    : 2026\-07\-01T21:31:37Z
In \[It\] at: self\_node\_remediation\_test.go:85
{code}

Cascading failure \-\- remaining 4 worker tests fail in setup:
{code}
\[FAILED\] Timed out after 300.000s.
Could not get boot time on target node
Unexpected error:
    :
    timed out waiting for the condition
In \[JustBeforeEach\] at: self\_node\_remediation\_test.go:77
{code}

Test summary:
{code}
Ran 6 of 6 Specs in 2549.858 seconds
FAIL\! \-\- 1 Passed | 5 Failed | 0 Pending | 0 Skipped
{code}

The single passing test is Control Plane Remediation, which targets a master node and successfully detects reboot.

h2. Evidence This Is Infrastructure, Not Code

* Identical failure across completely unrelated PRs: runner image change \(PR 308\), catalog metadata \(PR 311\), memory caching \(PR 310\), security hardening \(PR 309\)
* Same PR passes on one OCP version but fails on another \(e.g., PR 311 passes on 4.23 but fails on 4.22 and 5.0\)
* Control plane remediation always succeeds \-\- only worker node reboot detection fails
* Last merged PR \(PR 307, June 4\) passed all 3 OCP versions cleanly
* No code has been merged to main since June 4 \-\- all open PRs test against the same known\-good base

h2. Impact

* PR #308 \(runner image update\) is fully approved and merge\-ready but blocked by e2e failures
* PR #310 \(RHWA\-1026 memory fix\) has approved \+ lgtm but cannot validate on all OCP versions
* PR #311 \(catalog multi\-channel fix\) blocked on 4.22 and 5.0
* PR #309 \(security hardening\) blocked on all 3 versions

h2. Proposed Remediation

# Retest open PRs with /retest to check if failures are transient
# Investigate CI cluster worker node health on the medik8s\-aws IPI profile
# Check if OCP nightly streams for 4.22 and 5.0 have known instabilities that affect node reboot
# Consider adding retry logic or node pre\-validation in the e2e test framework to handle transient worker node issues
# If the issue is systemic, engage TRT/DPTP for cluster infrastructure investigation
# Review whether the privileged helper pod approach for detecting reboots needs hardening \(e.g., longer timeouts, alternative boot\-time detection\)

h2. Problem

Since June 2026, all open SNR PRs experience identical e2e test failures across OCP 4.22, 4.23, and 5.0. The failure pattern is consistent regardless of the PR's code changes, pointing to a CI infrastructure issue rather than code regressions.

5 of 6 e2e specs fail on every failing run. The only passing test is the Control Plane Remediation \(Resource Deletion Strategy\) targeting a master node.

h2. Failure Pattern

The root failure is in worker node remediation: the SNR operator triggers remediation but the worker node never reboots \(or the reboot is never detected\). The privileged helper pod that checks boot time returns Go's zero value \(0001\-01\-01T00:00:00Z\) after \~660 seconds, indicating it could never read the boot time from the target node post\-remediation.

After the first worker test fails, it leaves the node in a degraded/unreachable state, causing all 4 subsequent worker\-targeted specs to cascade\-fail in BeforeEach with: "Timed out after 300s. Could not get boot time on target node". The helper pod keeps being recreated every \~2.5 minutes but never succeeds.

An additional infra issue is observed: the src\-bundle step intermittently fails with "no image found in manifest list for architecture arm64" \(retries and succeeds\).

h1. _Problem_

5 of 6 e2e specs fail on every failing run. The only passing test is the Control Plane Remediation (Resource Deletion Strategy) targeting a master node.

h2. _Failure Pattern_

The root failure is in worker node remediation: the SNR operator triggers remediation but the worker node never reboots (or the reboot is never detected). The privileged helper pod that checks boot time returns Go's zero value (0001-01-01T00:00:00Z) after ~660 seconds, indicating it could never read the boot time from the target node post-remediation.

After the first worker test fails, it leaves the node in a degraded/unreachable state, causing all 4 subsequent worker-targeted specs to cascade-fail in BeforeEach with: "Timed out after 300s. Could not get boot time on target node". The helper pod keeps being recreated every ~2.5 minutes but never succeeds.

An additional infra issue is observed: the src-bundle step intermittently fails with "no image found in manifest list for architecture arm64" (retries and succeeds).

items.fromString: The medik8s step\-registry in openshift/release has identical OWNERS files duplicated across 20\+ directories. Adding a medik8s\-admins alias to OWNERS\_ALIASES centralizes team membership so future changes require editing only one file.
items.toString:
h3. Problem

The medik8s step-registry in openshift/release has identical OWNERS files duplicated across 20+ directories. Every new step-registry directory requires a copy of the same OWNERS file with the same list of 7 team members. When team membership changes (member joins/leaves), every file must be updated individually.

Example: PR [openshift/release#80372|https://github.com/openshift/release/pull/80372] added 6 identical copies of the same OWNERS file, one per new step-registry directory.

h3. Solution

Add a {{medik8s-admins}} alias to the openshift/release {{OWNERS_ALIASES}} file and update all step-registry OWNERS files to reference the alias instead of individual names. Future membership changes require editing only one file.

h3. Scope

* Step-registry OWNERS files (manually maintained) — will use the alias
* Config dir OWNERS files (auto-generated by ci-tools) — not affected, controlled by component repos

items.fromString:
Implement OLM upgrade tests for the SNR operator in the system-tests repository. Two upgrade scenarios are required:

*1. OCP Version Upgrade*
- Install SNR operator on OCP N-1
- Deploy SNR controller and DaemonSet agents, verify running
- Upgrade OCP to version N
- Verify SNR operator pod and DaemonSet agents survived the upgrade
- Verify CSV is still in Succeeded phase
- Run a remediation cycle (SelfNodeRemediation CR) to confirm end-to-end functionality post-upgrade

*2. Operator Version Upgrade (OLM channel upgrade)*
- Install SNR operator from the previous release channel/version via OLM
- Deploy SNR controller and DaemonSet agents
- Upgrade the operator to the current version (update Subscription channel or CatalogSource)
- Wait for OLM to roll out the new CSV
- Verify the new CSV reaches Succeeded phase and the old CSV is replaced
- Verify SNR controller and DaemonSet pods are restarted with the new image
- Run a remediation cycle to confirm end-to-end functionality post-upgrade

*Labels:* labels.TierUpgrade, labels.DisruptionDestructive, labels.FrequencyWeekly

Mirrors RHWA-842 (SBR upgrade test). Phase: 4 (Expansion)
items.toString:
Implement a combined OCP and operator upgrade test for SNR in the system-tests repository.

h3. Combined Upgrade Flow (single test)

The test validates the full customer upgrade path: OCP upgrade followed by operator upgrade, in one continuous flow.

# Install SNR operator from the previous release channel/version via OLM on OCP N-1
# Deploy SNR controller and DaemonSet agents, verify running
# Upgrade OCP from version N-1 to version N
# Verify SNR operator pod and DaemonSet agents survived the OCP upgrade
# Verify CSV is still in Succeeded phase
# Upgrade the operator to the current version (update Subscription channel or CatalogSource)
# Wait for OLM to roll out the new CSV
# Verify the new CSV reaches Succeeded phase and the old CSV is replaced
# Verify SNR controller and DaemonSet pods are restarted with the new image
# Run a remediation cycle (SelfNodeRemediation CR) to confirm end-to-end functionality

h3. CI Integration

* Add a dedicated Prow periodic job for upgrade testing (separate from the weekly smoke tests)
* The upgrade job needs access to two OCP versions and two operator catalog images

*Labels:* labels.TierUpgrade, labels.DisruptionDestructive, labels.FrequencyWeekly

Phase: 4 (Expansion)

items.fromString:
h2. Background

NMO has been kept unchanged for a few years while there was an upstream in-tree replacement (KEP-4212 [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4212|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4212] ), which was eventually closed in Jan 2026, and two new KEPs (EvictionRequest API + Node Lifecycle Conditions) are building lower-level primitives that NMO should adopt.
We have created an assessment report [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jE-mSkzHRzM6LfNy7HUSVCYp4Q6497qldtmDmFE6eqM|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jE-mSkzHRzM6LfNy7HUSVCYp4Q6497qldtmDmFE6eqM] for NMO's future when NMO has a 12-18 month window to be the only complete declarative node maintenance solution. There are alternatives, and Medik8's team should be aware of and follow the community changes.

h2. Upstream Community Tracking

h3. KEP-5683 Node Lifecycle Conditions

Track and adopt [KEP-5683|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5683] (Node Lifecycle Conditions), which as Phase 1 accepted for K8s 1.37 alpha, implementation PR already open [https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139993|https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139993] . Introduces well-known node conditions: _MaintenancePlanned_, _MaintenanceInProgress_, _DrainInProgress_, _Drained_, _GracefulNodeShutdownInProgress_.
_MaintenancePlanned_ and _MaintenanceInProgress_ directly affect NMO's lifecycle, and NMO should set these conditions during maintenance and consume them for better coordination with NHC.

KEP PR (merged): [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6161|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6161]
SIG Node announcement and call for feedback: [https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/sig-node/c/1RyyRqfRcG4/m/bkuSwPpEAgAJ|https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/sig-node/c/1RyyRqfRcG4/m/bkuSwPpEAgAJ]

h3. KEP-4563 EvictionRequest API

Track and plan adoption of [KEP-4563|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4563] (EvictionRequest API), which is alpha at K8s 1.37 (OCP 5.1), GA expected ~K8s 1.39 (OCP 5.3). This API provides coordinated graceful eviction with interceptor support. NMO should be an early adopter, providing real-world validation for the upstream API. Adoption would move NMO from wrapping kubectl drain to using upstream eviction primitives directly.

h3. WG Node Lifecycle Engagement

The Medik8s team should participate with [https://www.kubernetes.dev/community/community-groups/wg/node-lifecycle/|https://www.kubernetes.dev/community/community-groups/wg/node-lifecycle/|smart-link] to ensure upstream conditions align with NMO needs and provide real-world use cases (sequential drain bottleneck, NHC coordination, VM LiveMigrate).
Meeting agenda: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSSfiJatBYX7dhLTowYygDO6MK0K-NZ_L52bEZfcZqU|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSSfiJatBYX7dhLTowYygDO6MK0K-NZ_L52bEZfcZqU]
Use cases document: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EINvuVzEoRra0CKH6uQnOcQJVbd7ZnxT1bcyySN-r7c|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EINvuVzEoRra0CKH6uQnOcQJVbd7ZnxT1bcyySN-r7c]

h2. NMO Feature Gaps

Competitors like the NVIDIA maintenance operator [https://github.com/Mellanox/maintenance-operator|https://github.com/Mellanox/maintenance-operator] already ship coordination features NMO lacks. These are the gaps to close:

* _Implement parallel drain / async NodeMaintenance processing_ — NMO processes CRs sequentially (GitHub #164 [https://github.com/medik8s/node-maintenance-operator/issues/164|https://github.com/medik8s/node-maintenance-operator/issues/164] ). For clusters with 50+ nodes needing rolling maintenance, NMO becomes a bottleneck. Add maxParallelOperations or similar coordination. (Assessment Sections 3.1, 4.1)
* _Add emergency stop / global pause for maintenance operations_ — No cluster-wide mechanism to pause all active maintenance. Reversing a batch requires deleting CRs one by one. A global pause flag or maxUnavailable threshold would allow instant suspension of all drains without destroying the pending queue. (Assessment Section 3.6)
* [RHWA-288|https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA-288]: Enable Force Delete on Maintenance Mode
* [RHWA-1132|https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA-1132]: NMO Multi-arch Dockerfile and Makefile support

Background:
NMO has been kept unchanged for a few years while there was an upstream in\-tree replacement \(KEP\-4212 [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4212|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4212] \), that was eventually closed in Jan 2026, and two new KEPs \(EvictionRequest API \+ Node Lifecycle Conditions\) are building lower\-level primitives that NMO should adopt.
We have created an assessment report [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jE\-mSkzHRzM6LfNy7HUSVCYp4Q6497qldtmDmFE6eqM|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jE-mSkzHRzM6LfNy7HUSVCYp4Q6497qldtmDmFE6eqM] for NMO's future when NMO has a 12\-18 month window to be the only complete declarative node maintenance solution. There are alternatives and Medik8s team should be aware and follow the community changes.

h2. Upstream Community Tracking

h3. KEP\-5683 Node Lifecycle Conditions

Track and adopt KEP\-5683 \(Node Lifecycle Conditions\) [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5683|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5683] — Phase 1 accepted for K8s 1.37 alpha, implementation PR already open [https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139993|https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139993] . Introduces well\-known node conditions: MaintenancePlanned, MaintenanceInProgress, DrainInProgress, Drained, GracefulNodeShutdownInProgress. The first two map directly to NMO's lifecycle — NMO should set these conditions during maintenance and consume them for better coordination with NHC.

KEP PR \(merged\): [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6161|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6161]
SIG Node announcement and call for feedback: [https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/sig\-node/c/1RyyRqfRcG4/m/bkuSwPpEAgAJ|https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/sig-node/c/1RyyRqfRcG4/m/bkuSwPpEAgAJ]

h3. KEP\-4563 EvictionRequest API

Track and plan adoption of KEP\-4563 \(EvictionRequest API\) [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4563|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4563] — alpha at K8s 1.37 \(OCP 5.1\), GA expected \~K8s 1.39 \(OCP 5.3\). This API provides coordinated graceful eviction with interceptor support. NMO should be an early adopter, providing real\-world validation for the upstream API. Adoption would move NMO from wrapping kubectl drain to using upstream eviction primitives directly.

h3. WG Node Lifecycle Engagement

WG Node Lifecycle [https://www.kubernetes.dev/community/community\-groups/wg/node\-lifecycle/|https://www.kubernetes.dev/community/community-groups/wg/node-lifecycle/] — Red Hat has strong influence: Filip Krepinsky \(@atiratree\) is a co\-lead. Weekly meetings Monday 8am PT. NMO team should participate to ensure upstream conditions align with NMO needs and provide real\-world use cases \(sequential drain bottleneck, NHC coordination, VM LiveMigrate\).

Meeting agenda: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSSfiJatBYX7dhLTowYygDO6MK0K\-NZ\_L52bEZfcZqU|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSSfiJatBYX7dhLTowYygDO6MK0K-NZ_L52bEZfcZqU]

h2. NMO Feature Gaps

* _Implement parallel drain / async NodeMaintenance processing_ — NMO processes CRs sequentially \(GitHub #164 [https://github.com/medik8s/node\-maintenance\-operator/issues/164|https://github.com/medik8s/node-maintenance-operator/issues/164] \). For clusters with 50\+ nodes needing rolling maintenance, NMO becomes a bottleneck. Add maxParallelOperations or similar coordination. \(Assessment Sections 3.1, 4.1\)
* _Add emergency stop / global pause for maintenance operations_ — No cluster\-wide mechanism to pause all active maintenance. Reversing a batch requires deleting CRs one by one. A global pause flag or maxUnavailable threshold would allow instant suspension of all drains without destroying the pending queue. \(Assessment Section 3.6\)
* RHWA\-288 [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA\-288|https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA-288] : Enable Force Delete on Maintenance Mode
* RHWA\-1132 [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA\-1132|https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA-1132] : NMO Multi\-arch Dockerfile and Makefile support

Changes suggested by the NMO Assessment report [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jE\-mSkzHRzM6LfNy7HUSVCYp4Q6497qldtmDmFE6eqM|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jE-mSkzHRzM6LfNy7HUSVCYp4Q6497qldtmDmFE6eqM] \(June 2026\). NMO has received no feature investment in over two years, but its strategic position is stronger than its backlog suggests — the upstream in\-tree replacement \(KEP\-4212\) was closed, and NMO remains the only viable declarative node maintenance solution in the Kubernetes ecosystem.

h3. High Priority: KEP\-5683 Node Lifecycle Conditions

Track and adopt KEP\-5683 \(Node Lifecycle Conditions\) [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5683|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5683] — Phase 1 accepted for K8s 1.37 alpha, implementation PR already open [https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139993|https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139993] . Introduces well\-known node conditions: MaintenancePlanned, MaintenanceInProgress, DrainInProgress, Drained, GracefulNodeShutdownInProgress. The first two map directly to NMO's lifecycle — NMO should set these conditions during maintenance and consume them for better coordination with NHC.

KEP PR \(merged\): [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6161|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6161]
SIG Node announcement and call for feedback: [https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/sig\-node/c/1RyyRqfRcG4/m/bkuSwPpEAgAJ|https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/sig-node/c/1RyyRqfRcG4/m/bkuSwPpEAgAJ]

h3. High Priority: KEP\-4563 EvictionRequest API

Track and plan adoption of KEP\-4563 \(EvictionRequest API\) [https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4563|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4563] — alpha at K8s 1.37 \(OCP 5.1\), GA expected \~K8s 1.39 \(OCP 5.3\). This API provides coordinated graceful eviction with interceptor support. NMO should be an early adopter, providing real\-world validation for the upstream API. Adoption would move NMO from wrapping kubectl drain to using upstream eviction primitives directly.

h3. WG Node Lifecycle Engagement

WG Node Lifecycle [https://www.kubernetes.dev/community/community\-groups/wg/node\-lifecycle/|https://www.kubernetes.dev/community/community-groups/wg/node-lifecycle/] — Red Hat has strong influence: Filip Krepinsky \(@atiratree\) is a co\-lead, Ryan Hallisey \(@rthallisey\) authored KEP\-5683. Weekly meetings Monday 8am PT. NMO team should participate to ensure upstream conditions align with NMO needs and provide real\-world use cases \(sequential drain bottleneck, NHC coordination, VM LiveMigrate\).

Meeting agenda: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSSfiJatBYX7dhLTowYygDO6MK0K\-NZ\_L52bEZfcZqU|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSSfiJatBYX7dhLTowYygDO6MK0K-NZ_L52bEZfcZqU]
Use cases document: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EINvuVzEoRra0CKH6uQnOcQJVbd7ZnxT1bcyySN\-r7c|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EINvuVzEoRra0CKH6uQnOcQJVbd7ZnxT1bcyySN-r7c]

h3. Suggested Tickets

The following items should be created as Stories under this Epic:

* _Implement parallel drain / async NodeMaintenance processing_ — NMO processes CRs sequentially \(GitHub #164 [https://github.com/medik8s/node\-maintenance\-operator/issues/164|https://github.com/medik8s/node-maintenance-operator/issues/164]\). For clusters with 50\+ nodes needing rolling maintenance, NMO becomes a bottleneck. Add maxParallelOperations or similar coordination. The NVIDIA maintenance operator [https://github.com/Mellanox/maintenance\-operator|https://github.com/Mellanox/maintenance-operator] provides an architecture reference. \(Assessment Sections 3.1, 4.1\)
* _Add emergency stop / global pause for maintenance operations_ — No cluster\-wide mechanism to pause all active maintenance. Reversing a batch requires deleting CRs one by one. A global pause flag or maxUnavailable threshold would allow instant suspension of all drains without destroying the pending queue. \(Assessment Section 3.6\)
* _Graduate NMO API from v1beta1 to v1_ — NMO has been stable for 4\+ years. v1beta1 signals not\-ready when the operator clearly is. Aligns with Daniel's concern about alpha/beta APIs across the suite. \(Assessment Section 8\)
* _Participate in WG Node Lifecycle and provide NMO use cases_ — Low effort, high strategic value. Contribute NMO's real\-world maintenance patterns to the upstream use cases document.

* RHWA\-1132 [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA\-1132|https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHWA-1132] : NMO Multi\-arch Dockerfile and Makefile support

items.fromString:
Tracking and analyzing the usage (or popularity) of our operators by looking on the attraction from our website, [Medik8s.io|https://www.medik8s.io/], could help us to better understand some of the following ideas:
 * How many people search Medik8s.io?
 * Page views and unique page views
 * Nice to have: Who is our audience (age, demography and etc.)

The top three free options are [Google Analytics|https://developers.google.com/analytics] (GA), [Clicky|https://clicky.com/] and [Matomo|https://matomo.org/] (and on [Github|https://github.com/matomo-org/matomo]). 
Google Analytics is the standard analytics tool which is free and easy to setup. It might be a little bit complex for rookies and the page-view results are approximation.

Clicky and Matomo are both privacy-focused (GDPR-compliant), and they share additional features to GA like heatmaps. 
Clicky has real-time reporting and is easier to setup in comparison to Matomo.
Matomo is open source with data ownership (you own 100% of the data Matomo finds), and without data sampling (tracks all user data to offer accurate results).

Links for GA:
 * Videos: [https://www.youtube.com/@GoogleAnalytics]
 * *Google Analytics Demos & Tools: [https://ga-dev-tools.google/]*

 * Our operators are not collecting any telemetry data regarding their usage, thus collecting analytics from our website should be good start to get insights about their usage until they will begin collecting telemetry data.

Matomo is open source with data ownership (you own 100% of the data Matomo finds), and without data sampling (tracks all user data to offer accurate results).

*What do we have?*

Currently we have some CI tests before and after PRs in Medik8s which includes OCP _CI-Operator_ for Medik8s in [https://github.com/openshift/release/tree/master/ci-operator/config/medik8s] with three tests:
 * Images (IDK what creates this test)
 * ci-index (for more see [here|https://docs.ci.openshift.org/docs/how-tos/testing-operator-sdk-operators/#validating-bundle-and-index-builds]).
 * e2e tests

In addition, we use _Github Actions_ to build our operators before merging PR (see in [NHC pre-submit.yaml|https://github.com/medik8s/node-healthcheck-operator/blob/main/.github/workflows/pre-submit.yaml]) and when it is merged we have a task which rebuild it and push it to Quay.io (see in [NHC post-submit.yaml|https://github.com/medik8s/node-healthcheck-operator/blob/main/.github/workflows/post-submit.yaml]).

*What we could add?*
 * K8s CI (in addition to OCP CI) - Test our operators upstream (Medik8s) with a Kubernetes cluster (kind/minikube).
 * Review new _Github Actions_ (e.g. [dependency-review-action|https://github.com/actions/dependency-review-action])
 * _Github_ _templates_ for PRs and Issues?
 * Operator Upgrade Testing ? (It is documented in [OCP CI|https://docs.ci.openshift.org/docs/how-tos/testing-operator-sdk-operators/#operator-upgrade-testing] but we might have something similar in K8s CI).
 * Different cloud provider for E2e tests are flaky. Maybe it is related to running it in AWS cluster? We could add e2e test in Azure/GCP for better inspection (maybe as an optional test).
 * -Multiple OCP versions (old and new).- We are already supporting multiple OCP releases for e2e tests since the beginning of 2023.
 * Upgrade of operator and upgrade of OCP.

*Open Question:*
 * Do we have CI tests for must-gather containers (NMO and SNR/NHC)?

Prepare and submit a CNCF Sandbox application for Medik8s. Entry\-level CNCF tier that provides neutral governance, trademark protection, and increased visibility.

Prerequisites: Community Phase 1 \(GitHub changes\), Phase 2 \(Helm support\), Phase 3 \(upstream\-first decision\).

CNCF Sandbox requirements:
\- GOVERNANCE.md, MAINTAINERS.md, Code of Conduct
\- SECURITY.md \(vulnerability reporting process\)
\- ADOPTERS.md \(outreach to known vanilla K8s users\)
\- Public roadmap \(GitHub project board\)
\- Trademark donated to Linux Foundation
\- 2 TOC sponsors

Scope:
\- Create governance docs
\- Build ADOPTERS.md
\- Articulate Medik8s vs RHWA product separation for CNCF
\- Obtain Red Hat legal approval for trademark donation to LF
\- Submit CNCF Sandbox application

Reference: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/16F15\-p\_vypPA\-UtFJsAfXl6EVDdRjubIvOMtvzSVcn0|https://docs.google.com/document/d/16F15-p_vypPA-UtFJsAfXl6EVDdRjubIvOMtvzSVcn0] \(Tab: CNCF Sandbox\)

Add Kind\-based e2e CI to all operators to ensure they work on vanilla Kubernetes — a prerequisite for confident upstream releases to the community OperatorHub.

Current state:
\- NHC: Full e2e on Kind \(GitHub Actions\)
\- NMO: Scorecard only \(no functional e2e\)
\- FAR: Scorecard only \(no functional e2e\)
\- SNR: Makefile targets exist but no CI automation
\- MDR: OCP\-dependent \(machine.openshift.io APIs\)
\- SBR: TBD

Scope:
\- Standardize Makefile targets across all 6 operators \(test, test\-e2e, verify\)
\- Add Kind\-based e2e CI to NMO, FAR, SNR, SBR using NHC's setup as template
\- Validate community bundle format in CI

h3. Current state

* NHC: Full e2e on Kind (GitHub Actions)
* NMO: Scorecard only (no functional e2e)
* FAR: Scorecard only (no functional e2e)
* SNR: Makefile targets exist but no CI automation
* MDR: OCP-dependent (machine.openshift.io APIs)
* SBR: TBD

h3. Scope

* Standardize Makefile targets across all 6 operators (test, test-e2e, verify)
* Add Kind-based e2e CI to NMO, FAR, SNR, SBR using NHC's setup as template
* Validate community bundle format in CI

Based on OPGM-8 template.

This Epic tracks work to ensure the Self Node Remediation (SNR) operator's latest 4.22-compatible release is also certified for OpenShift 5.0, enabling seamless platform upgrades without operator updates.

Parent Outcome: OCPSTRAT-2857 - All OLM-managed Red Hat operators support OpenShift 5.0 at launch

Parent Feature: RHWA-785 - OpenShift 5.0 Operator Compatibility Requirements for RHWA

Goal: Latest SNR operator release on OCP 4.22 (v0.12.0) ALSO works on OCP 5.0. Target release for OCP 4.23/5.0: v0.13.0

Customer Value: Customers on OCP 4.22 can upgrade to 5.0 without updating the SNR operator

Key fact: OCP 4.23 and 5.0 both ship K8s 1.36. UBI 9 stays as the base through OCP 5.2. No base image migration is needed for OCP 5.0 — existing UBI 9 images work on RHCOS 10.

Decision Tree: Standard vs Exception Path

Q1: Does SNR have low-level kernel or OS dependencies?

YES. SNR uses:
- Host PID namespace sharing (hostPID: true) for process inspection
- /proc filesystem access to detect unhealthy processes
- Watchdog device interaction (/dev/watchdog) for hardware-based remediation
- Direct node reboot via systemd API

Decision: Exception Path (requires verification that host-level features work identically on RHCOS 10)

Q2: Can we backport OCP 5.0 support to the 4.22 release?

LIKELY YES. SNR's host dependencies are stable Linux kernel features that shouldn't change between RHCOS 9 and RHCOS 10. However, testing is critical.

Q3: Does SNR use Kubernetes APIs deprecated in 1.36?

-TODO — needs audit. SNR uses:
- Standard K8s APIs (apps/v1, core/v1, rbac)
- machine.openshift.io/v1beta1 — Machine API (verify availability in OCP 5.0)
- Lease API (coordination.k8s.io/v1) for peer health tracking-

  *No.* SNR uses only stable K8s v1 APIs (apps/v1, core/v1, rbac/v1, coordination/v1). None are deprecated in K8s 1.36.

  The OpenShift-specific {{machine.openshift.io/v1beta1}} API is confirmed available in OCP 5.0 (verified via [MDR e2e tests|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/pr-logs/pull/medik8s_machine-deletion-remediation/179/pull-ci-medik8s-machine-deletion-remediation-main-5.0-openshift-e2e/2069693837667733504]). 


Deliverables

Identification
[ ] Latest SNR release certified for OCP 4.22 identified (version: v0.12.0)
[x] Decision made: Exception path (host-level dependencies require RHCOS 10 verification)
[x] Base image decision: Stay on UBI 9 (UBI 10 migration deferred to OCP 5.5)

Testing - Fresh Install on OCP 5.0
[ ] Operator installs successfully from OperatorHub
[ ] All operator pods reach Ready state
[ ] DaemonSet pods running on all nodes (RHCOS 10)
[ ] Watchdog device access working (/dev/watchdog on RHCOS 10)
[ ] /proc filesystem inspection working
[ ] Peer health detection working
[ ] Full regression test suite passing
[ ] Performance testing completed

Testing - Upgrade Path (4.22 -> 5.0)
[ ] Operator installed on OCP 4.22 cluster
[ ] Platform upgraded from 4.22 to 5.0
[ ] Operator survives platform upgrade without updates
[ ] DaemonSet pods successfully restart on RHCOS 10 nodes
[ ] All workloads functioning after platform upgrade
[ ] Watchdog remediation verified on RHCOS 10
[ ] No data loss or corruption

Testing - Day 2 Operations on OCP 5.0
[ ] Operator upgrade tested (to newer version)
[ ] Configuration changes tested
[ ] Scaling tested (add/remove nodes)
[ ] Node remediation tested (software reboot, watchdog reboot)
[ ] Peer-based remediation tested

RHCOS 10 Specific Testing
[ ] Watchdog device availability verified on RHCOS 10
[ ] /dev/watchdog permissions correct
[ ] systemd reboot API working on RHCOS 10
[ ] /proc filesystem structure unchanged
[ ] Host PID namespace behavior identical
[ ] Security context compatibility (privileged DaemonSet)
[ ] Kernel version differences documented (if any affect SNR)

Metadata & Certification
[ ] Operator CSV updated with OCP 5.0 support
[ ] minKubeVersion/maxKubeVersion allows both 4.22 and 5.0 (K8s 1.35 and 1.36)
[ ] Supported OCP versions explicitly lists 4.22 and 5.0
[ ] Operator submitted for OCP 5.0 certification
[ ] Certification passed
[ ] No olm.maxOpenShiftVersion blocking 5.0

Documentation
[ ] Compatibility matrix updated to show 4.22 and 5.0 support
[ ] Release notes mention OCP 5.0 compatibility
[ ] RHCOS 10 compatibility explicitly documented
[ ] Upgrade docs include 5.0 considerations
[ ] Known issues documented (if any)
[ ] Watchdog behavior on RHCOS 10 documented

Coordination
[ ] QE notified and testing scheduled (RHCOS 10 testing critical)
[ ] Docs team notified of compatibility updates
[ ] Support team briefed on 5.0 compatibility and RHCOS 10
[ ] OperatorHub team coordinated with for catalog updates
[ ] Completion announcement sent

Testing Checklist

Pre-Testing:
[ ] OCP 5.0 Beta/RC cluster available
[x] Latest 4.22 SNR release identified (v0.12.0)
[ ] Test plan reviewed and approved
[ ] RHCOS 10 test nodes available

Fresh Install Tests (OCP 5.0):
[ ] Operator installs successfully from OperatorHub
[ ] All operator pods reach Ready state
[ ] DaemonSet running on RHCOS 10 nodes
[ ] Operator CRDs created correctly
[ ] Basic functionality working
[ ] Watchdog accessible (/dev/watchdog)

Upgrade Path Tests:
[ ] Operator installed on OCP 4.22 cluster (RHCOS 9)
[ ] Platform upgraded from 4.22 to 5.0 (RHCOS 9 -> RHCOS 10)
[ ] Operator survives platform upgrade
[ ] DaemonSet pods restart successfully on RHCOS 10
[ ] Operator still functioning after upgrade
[ ] Watchdog remediation works on RHCOS 10
[ ] Workloads still functioning
[ ] No unexpected errors in operator logs

Regression Tests:
[ ] Full regression suite executed on OCP 5.0
[ ] All tests passing (or known issues documented)
[ ] Performance benchmarks met
[ ] Remediation latency unchanged on RHCOS 10

Day 2 Operations (OCP 5.0):
[ ] Operator upgrade tested (to newer version)
[ ] Configuration changes tested
[ ] Node scaling tested (add/remove nodes with RHCOS 10)
[ ] Software reboot remediation tested
[ ] Watchdog-based remediation tested
[ ] Peer health detection tested

Compatibility Tests:
[ ] Kubernetes API version compatibility verified (K8s 1.36)
[ ] CRD version compatibility confirmed
[ ] No deprecated API usage
[ ] Works with expected Kubernetes 1.36 features
[ ] machine.openshift.io/v1beta1 availability confirmed

RHCOS-Specific Tests:
[ ] Watchdog device present and accessible
[ ] /proc filesystem structure verified
[ ] systemd reboot API functional
[ ] Security contexts work (privileged, hostPID)
[ ] Kernel differences identified (if any)

FBC Catalog
[ ] OCP 5.0 catalog entry created for SNR
[ ] Base: ose-operator-registry-rhel9:v5.0 (OpenShift stays on UBI 9)
[ ] releases.yaml and operator-versions.yaml updated
[ ] Existing rhel9 operator images referenced

Open Questions

K8s API audit: Does SNR use any APIs deprecated/removed in K8s 1.36? Specifically machine.openshift.io/v1beta1 — verify availability in OCP 5.0.

RHCOS 10 watchdog: Are there any changes to watchdog device behavior, permissions, or availability in RHCOS 10 vs RHCOS 9?

RHCOS 10 /proc: Are there any /proc filesystem changes that could affect SNR's health detection logic?

RHCOS 10 systemd: Any changes to systemd reboot API between RHCOS 9 and 10?

OCP 5.0 test clusters: When will beta/RC clusters with RHCOS 10 be available for testing?

OCP CI Prow: When will OCP 5.0 Prow build roots be available?

Security context: Will privileged DaemonSets with hostPID still be allowed on OCP 5.0, or are there new pod security standard restrictions?

Communication Template

Email Subject
[SNR] - OpenShift 5.0 Compatibility Confirmed

Email Body

Team,

I'm pleased to confirm that Self Node Remediation (SNR) operator version [X.Y.Z] has been certified for OpenShift 5.0 and is compatible with our latest 4.22 release.

Compatibility Details:
 * Operator Version: [X.Y.Z]
 * Certified for: OCP 4.22 and OCP 5.0
 * Upgrade Path: Seamless (no operator update required)
 * Exception Status: Exception (host-level dependencies verified on RHCOS 10)
 * Base Image: UBI 9 (no migration needed — UBI 9 runs on RHCOS 10)
 * UBI 10 migration deferred to OCP 5.5
 * RHCOS 10 Compatibility: Verified (watchdog, /proc, systemd, hostPID)

This means customers running SNR on OpenShift 4.22 can upgrade to OpenShift 5.0 without needing to update their operator, reducing upgrade complexity and risk.

Note: SNR's host-level features (watchdog device, /proc inspection, hostPID) have been thoroughly tested and verified to work identically on RHCOS 10.

Documentation:
 * Compatibility Matrix: [LINK]
 * Release Notes: [LINK]
 * Upgrade Guide: [LINK]
 * RHCOS 10 Compatibility Notes: [LINK]

Available in OperatorHub: [DATE]

Questions? Contact: [OWNER]

Instructions
Replace all [PLACEHOLDERS] with your actual information
Send to your team, stakeholders, Product Marketing, and Support

[ ] Completion announcement sent using communication template

Q1: Does SNR have low-level kernel or OS dependencies?

- Host PID namespace sharing (hostPID: true) for process inspection
- /proc filesystem access to detect unhealthy processes
- Watchdog device interaction (/dev/watchdog) for hardware-based remediation
- Direct node reboot via systemd API

Decision: Exception Path (requires verification that host-level features work identically on RHCOS 10)

 * Base Image: UBI 9 (no migration needed — UBI 9 runs on RHCOS 10)
 * UBI 10 migration deferred to OCP 5.5
 * RHCOS 10 Compatibility: Verified (watchdog, /proc, systemd, hostPID)

This means customers running SNR on OpenShift 4.22 can upgrade to OpenShift 5.0 without needing to update their operator, reducing upgrade complexity and risk.

Note: SNR's host-level features (watchdog device, /proc inspection, hostPID) have been thoroughly tested and verified to work identically on RHCOS 10.

items.toString: This work item relates to ECOPROJECT-1008

h3. Background

All 6 Medik8s operators in {{community-operators-prod}} use the legacy SQLite-based catalog format. The pipeline flags a {{check_using_fbc}} warning on every submission PR. FBC (File Based Catalog) provides declarative, version-controlled catalog definitions and is the format the community pipeline is moving toward.

h3. PRs with the warning

||*PR*||*Operator*||*Version*||
|[#10058|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/pull/10058]|node-healthcheck-operator|0.12.0|
|[#10059|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/pull/10059]|self-node-remediation|0.13.0|
|[#10060|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/pull/10060]|fence-agents-remediation|0.8.0|
|[#10061|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/pull/10061]|node-maintenance-operator|0.21.0|
|[#10062|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/pull/10062]|machine-deletion-remediation|0.7.0|
|[#10071|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/pull/10071]|storage-based-remediation|0.3.0|

h3. Scope

# *FBC onboarding PRs* to community-operators-prod — one per operator (6 total)
# *Update community-release.sh automation* — after FBC migration, new releases also need to update catalog-templates and regenerate catalogs

h3. FBC onboarding per operator

In a local fork of community-operators-prod, for each operator:

* Run {{make fbc-onboarding}} (auto-detects OCP versions from what's already published)
* Generates {{catalog-templates/basic.yaml}} — FBC template (channels, upgrade graph, bundle digests)
* Updates {{ci.yaml}} with {{fbc: enabled: true}} + catalog_mapping
* Renders {{catalogs/v4.xx/<name>/catalog.yaml}} per OCP version

SBR also needs a ci.yaml created first (missing updateGraph).

h3. Automation update

Current automation ({{medik8s/.github/scripts/community-release.sh}} + {{release_community_bundle.yaml}}) only creates bundle directories. After FBC migration, new releases also need to:

* Add a new {{olm.bundle}} entry to {{catalog-templates/basic.yaml}}
* Update {{olm.channel}} entries with the new version's upgrade edge
* Run {{make catalogs}} to regenerate catalogs from the updated template

h3. Open question

The downstream FBC (rhwa-fbc on GitLab) uses a multi-config approach (operator-versions.yaml, releases.yaml, gen_template.sh). The upstream community-operators-prod FBC uses a simpler per-operator catalog-templates/basic.yaml. Should we align the template format/tooling, or keep them separate since they serve different purposes (product vs community)?

h3. References

* [FBC onboarding guide|https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/operator-pipelines/users/fbc_onboarding/]
* [FBC discussion|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/discussions/5031]
* [community-release.sh|https://github.com/medik8s/.github/blob/main/scripts/community-release.sh]

Update Dockerfile and Makefile in [medik8s/storage-based-remediation|https://github.com/medik8s/storage-based-remediation] to support multi-architecture builds per [Operator SDK best practices|https://sdk.operatorframework.io/docs/advanced-topics/multi-arch/].

h3. Changes Required

* *Dockerfile:* Use {{ARG TARGETARCH}} and replace hardcoded {{amd64}} with {{$TARGETARCH}} in Go download. Add {{--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM}} to builder stage.
* *Makefile:* Add {{docker-buildx}} target with {{PLATFORMS}} variable per SDK v1.34.0 pattern. Default {{PLATFORMS ?= linux/amd64}}, opt-in multi-arch via {{PLATFORMS=linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/ppc64le,linux/s390x}}.
* *Node affinity:* Add {{requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution}} with {{kubernetes.io/arch}} and {{kubernetes.io/os}} in {{config/manager/manager.yaml}}.
* *Bundle validation:* Run {{operator-sdk bundle validate ./bundle --select-optional name=multiarch}}.
* *Status:* SBR already has {{ARG TARGETARCH}} in Dockerfile and {{PLATFORMS}} + {{buildx}} in Makefile. Remaining work: uncomment node affinity TODO in {{config/manager/manager.yaml}} and run bundle validation.

h3. References

* [Operator SDK Multi-Architecture Docs|https://sdk.operatorframework.io/docs/advanced-topics/multi-arch/]

items.fromString:
Make upstream Medik8s operator builds multi-architecture capable. Covers Dockerfile and Makefile changes to support cross-compilation and multi-platform container images.

Based on community request [fence-agents-remediation#207|https://github.com/medik8s/fence-agents-remediation/issues/207] and the guidance in [razo7's comment|https://github.com/medik8s/fence-agents-remediation/issues/207#issuecomment-4706057301]. The Go binary side is partially addressed by FAR PR #199. The remaining work is:

* *Dockerfile:* Use ARG TARGETARCH and --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM for cross-compilation. Replace hardcoded amd64 Go download with $TARGETARCH.
* *Makefile:* Add docker-buildx target with PLATFORMS variable (default linux/amd64, opt-in multi-arch).
* *Verify RPM availability:* fence-agents-* packages for aarch64 in CentOS Stream 9 highavailability repo.

h3. Scope

One task per operator: FAR, NHC, SNR, MDR, NMO, SBR. Operator images are the priority. Bundle images are arch-independent (FROM scratch). Catalog images also need multi-arch support (opm is arch-specific).

[catalog.redhat.com|https://catalog.redhat.com] labels will regress from correct v0.2.0 to incorrect if not fixed before next release.
* *Documentation MRs* [\!250|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/telco-team-documentation/workload-availability-for-red-hat-openshift/-/merge_requests/250]/[\!251|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/telco-team-documentation/workload-availability-for-red-hat-openshift/-/merge_requests/251]: ~45 incorrect usages — "Storage-based" (lowercase b) in customer-facing docs

items.toString: This work item links to "medik8s/system-tests#52: tests/snr: add 5 destructive remediation tests (worker + master) (Web Link)"

items.fromString:
Core remediation tests that stop kubelet on nodes and validate the SNR remediation flow via MHC/NHC detection. Destructive — nodes reboot during the test. Failed on x86 edge119 (may be env-specific). Requires SSH access to nodes and longer timeouts (~15 min per remediation cycle).

Source file: test_snr_cli.py → classes TestHealthDetectionForWorkersUsingSnr, TestHealthDetectionForControlPlanesUsingSnr

h3. Tests in Scope

Test 5 — test_snr_must_gather (OCP-50774): Runs RHWA must-gather image, verifies SNR-specific data files are present in collected output. Labels: operator:snr, tier:acceptance, frequency:weekly, component:diagnostics. Non-destructive.

Test 7 — test_snr_with_stop_kubelet_for_worker (OCP-52417/OCP-52416): Stops kubelet on worker → MHC or NHC detects unhealthy → SNR creates remediation CR → node reboots → recovers. Destructive.

Test 8 — test_remediation_strategy_resource_deletion (OCP-50772): NHC-only. Deploys test app, stops kubelet on worker → ResourceDeletion strategy → app pod rescheduled to healthy node. Destructive.

Test 9 — test_remediation_strategy_out_of_service_taint (OCP-61594): NHC-only. Deploys test app, stops kubelet on worker → OutOfServiceTaint strategy → app pod rescheduled. Destructive.

Test 10 — test_snr_with_stop_kubelet_for_master (OCP-55058/OCP-55059): Stops kubelet on master → MHC or NHC detects → SNR remediates with NoExecute taints → master reboots and recovers. Destructive.

Test 11 — test_snr_with_stop_kubelet_for_master_and_worker (OCP-56069): NHC-only. Stops kubelet on master AND worker simultaneously → both remediated concurrently. Destructive.

h3. Files to Create/Modify

* tests/snr-operator/tests/worker_remediation.go — worker kubelet-stop tests (Tests 7-9)
* tests/snr-operator/tests/master_remediation.go — master kubelet-stop tests (Tests 10-11)
* May need node operation helpers (stop_kubelet, wait_for_reboot) — check tests/internal/ or port from SBR (see RHWA-874)

h3. Prerequisites

Phase 1 completed. Node operation helpers available. SSH or oc debug node/ access. 3+ worker nodes for Tests 8-9. Must-gather image available for Test 5.

h3. Done When

All 5 tests pass on x86 with both MHC and NHC detection modes. ARM as stretch goal.

items.toString: This work item links to "medik8s/storage-based-remediation#69: fix: Prevent ghost peers and stale node map restart loops (Web Link)"

items.fromString:
When you delete and recreate a StorageBasedRemediationConfig, the shared storage file that tracks which node "owns" which SBD slot is not cleaned up. When the new agents start, they find old entries in that file from the previous run. The peer-monitor sees those entries as nodes that have gone silent, flags them as unhealthy, and the liveness probe kills the pod. The pod restarts in a loop until the stale entries age out - which can take many minutes. On a healthy cluster this self-heals, but the operator gives the impression of being broken after a routine recreate.

*Scenario #1*

# SBRC sbr-config is created. The sbr-device-init job runs and initializes the shared PVC (/dev/sbr/sbr-device). Each agent registers its node in the on-disk node map
({{/dev/sbr/sbr-device-nodemap}}), keyed by a node ID derived from a hash of the node hostname.
# SBRC is deleted. The controller tears down the DaemonSet and agents shut down gracefully. The PVC object is deleted, but with {{reclaimPolicy: Retain}} the underlying NFS export and node map file on disk are preserved. The state only appears clean at the Kubernetes layer.
# SBRC is recreated with the same spec. The operator provisions a new PVC, runs {{sbr-device-init}}, and starts the DaemonSet. The init job initializes the raw SBD slots but does not reset
the node map file - it inherits whatever was written by previous agents or left in a partial state.
# Agents start. Each agent derives its node ID from a hash of its node hostname - the same hash as before, so the same node IDs are reused. The agent reads the on-disk node map and
finds entries from the previous run: stale node IDs with old heartbeat timestamps, some of which no longer correspond to any active node in the current cluster (e.g. a node that was in a
prior run but now has a different ID assignment).
# The peer-monitor thread starts and immediately checks peer liveness. A stale entry has a heartbeat timestamp ~105 seconds old. The peer timeout is also ~105 seconds. The peer-monitor
flags that stale entry as unhealthy: {{"Peer node became unhealthy", nodeID:1, timeSinceLastSeen:105s.}}
# The liveness probe ({{grep -l sbr-agent /proc/*/cmdline}}) runs on schedule. The probe fails  - not because the agent process is gone, but because the container was already killed by a
prior probe failure in the tight restart loop during the stale-entry convergence window.
# The pod on the affected node restarts. Each restart cycle partially refreshes the node map as other agents write fresh heartbeats. After 11 restarts (~10 minutes), the stale entries
age out, the map reflects only live nodes, and the pod stabilizes.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Install SBR operator and create an SBRC
# Wait for all agents to reach 1/1 Running.
# Delete the SBRC: {{oc delete storagebasedremediationconfig sbr-config -n sbr-system}}
# Wait for all pods and the DaemonSet to be gone.
# Recreate the SBRC with the same spec.
# Watch the pods: {{oc get pods -n sbr-system -w}}

Expected: All agent pods reach 1/1 Running within 1-2 minutes with 0 or at most 1 restart (image pull + normal startup).

  Actual: One or more agent pods enter a restart loop (observed: 11 restarts on a single node, ~10 minutes to stabilize). The SBRC condition Ready is delayed until the stale entries
  converge.

----

  *Root cause*

  The sbr-device-init job initializes SBD slots on creation but does not clear the node map file. On deletion, the controller does not run any cleanup job against the shared PVC before
  removing it. If the PVC is retained or a new PVC is backed by the same underlying storage, the stale node map is inherited by the next SBRC.

----

  *Fix recommendation*

# (Primary) During SBRC deletion, before tearing down the DaemonSet, run a cleanup job (or reuse sbr-device-init with a wipe mode) that zeros out the node map file on the shared PVC.
# (Defensive) At agent startup, cross-check node map entries against the Kubernetes nodes currently matching the SBRC's nodeSelector. Prune entries for nodes that are not active targets
before the peer-monitor starts.

items.fromString:
The SBR operator exposes metrics on both the controller manager (8443) and agent DaemonSet (8080) but none of it reaches Prometheus. Three things are missing, all required for scraping to work - NHC has all three correct.

|| ||NHC||SBR operator (Controller manager)||SBR agent (DaemonSet)||

items.fromString:
The SBR controller manager and agent DaemonSet do not declare container ports in their pod specs, unlike NHC which properly declares {{containerPort: 8443 (https)}} on its controller manager.

*Steps to reproduce:*

Agent DaemonSet (sbr-system):
{{oc get pods -n sbr-system -l app=sbr-agent \}}
{{  -o jsonpath='{range .items[0]}{range .spec.containers[*]}{.name}: {.ports}{"\n"}{end}{end}'}}

Controller manager (openshift-workload-availability):
{{oc get pods -n openshift-workload-availability -l app.kubernetes.io/name=sbr-operator \}}
{{  -o jsonpath='{range .items[0]}{range .spec.containers[*]}{.name}: {.ports}{"\n"}{end}{end}'}}

Both return empty - no ports declared.

*Expected*: {{containerPort: 8080}} declared on the agent container, {{containerPort: 8443}} on the controller manager container, consistent with operator-sdk scaffolding defaults and NHC's implementation.

*Actual*: No ports declared on either component. Port 8080 is live on agent pods (confirmed via {{curl localhost:8080/metrics}} exec) but undeclared.

*Impact:*

* Ports are invisible in oc describe pod output
* ServiceMonitors/PodMonitors cannot reference ports by name — must hardcode port numbers
* Indicates metrics were never intentionally wired for observability on either component

Hi Jim,

I reviewed the KCS ([https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7143062|https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7143062]) — both options are valid and safe to suggest to the customer:

* *Option 1 (direct oc patch)* — simple, good for single clusters.
* *Option 2 (ConfigurationPolicy)* — better for RHACM/ZTP fleets, can be cleanly removed once the fix ships.

The customer should be aware that with ScheduleAnyway, both manager replicas may co-locate on the same node (reduced HA posture) until v0.11.1 becomes available in their OCP catalog. On a 2-worker cluster this is a reasonable trade-off since the hard constraint was the root cause of the deadlock.

We're still targeting the patch release (v0.11.1 in OCP 4.18/4.19 indexes + upgrade graph fix) in the rhwa-4.22-1 timeframe.

items.fromString:
*Description of problem:*

{noformat}<Describe the During an EUS multi-hop upgrade path (RHOCP 4.18.27 -> 4.19.23 -> 4.20.14) managed via RHACM ZTP, the Self Node Remediation (SNR) operator gets stuck in an unrecoverable "InstallCheckFailed" timeout state during its transition from v0.10.2 to v0.11.0.

RCA: it seems to be:
SNR v0.11.0 introduces strict 'topologySpreadConstraints' with 'whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule' and scales the manager replicas from 1 to 2. 

Because the deployment utilizes the default 'maxSurge' strategy, the cluster attempts to spin up the new v0.11.0 pods before evicting the legacy v0.10.2 pods. In environments with small footprints (such as clusters with exactly 2 schedulable worker nodes), the existing v0.10.2 pods occupy 100% of the available scheduling slots. 

Consequently, the new v0.11.0 pods cannot satisfy the anti-affinity/spread constraints and remain permanently in a 'Pending' state. This triggers an OLM installation timeout after exceeding the progress deadline.

Proof & Log Evidence
The scheduler explicitly drops the pods with the following constraint message:
0/8 nodes are available: 2 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master: }, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node.ocs.openshift.io/storage: true}.

A side-by-side verification confirms that SNR v0.10.2 did not enforce this constraint, while v0.11.0 introduces it as a hard rule, breaking the upgrade path for 2-node worker topologies. 

Requested Action / Fix
Please backport the deployment rollout strategy fix already present in SNR v0.12 (upstream main branch) into the v0.11 stream. The fix enforces:
* maxSurge: 0
* maxUnavailable: 1

This layout forces a "one-out, one-in" eviction flow that clears a node slot *before* attempting to schedule the new replica, resolving the deadlock.problem here>{noformat}

*Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):*

{noformat}self-node-remediation-operator v0.11.0 (on RHOCP 4.20.14){noformat}

*How reproducible:*

{noformat}Always (100% reproducible on clusters with exactly 2 schedulable worker nodes during the upgrade path from v0.10.2).{noformat}

*Steps to Reproduce:*

{noformat}1. Deploy Self Node Remediation (SNR) operator version v0.10.2 on an OpenShift cluster with only 2 schedulable worker nodes (e.g., 3 Masters, 3 Storage, 2 Workers topology).
2. Trigger a cluster upgrade or operator subscription upgrade to target SNR v0.11.0.
3. Observe the OLM installation phase and check the scheduling status of the new controller-manager pods.{noformat}

*Actual results:*

{noformat}The upgrade process hangs and eventually times out into an 'InstallCheckFailed' state. The new SNR v0.11.0 manager pods remain indefinitely in a 'Pending' state due to unsatisfied topology spread constraints, as the legacy v0.10.2 pods continue to occupy the only 2 available worker nodes.{noformat}

*Expected results:*

{noformat}The operator upgrade rollout should execute smoothly without blocking itself. The deployment strategy should clean up/evict old replicas sequentially (e.g., via maxSurge: 0 / maxUnavailable: 1) to free up node space before trying to schedule the newer v0.11.0 replicas on small-footprint environments.{noformat}

*Additional info:*

{noformat}The issue has already been resolved in upstream version SNR v0.12 by adjusting the rollout strategy requirements. 
A backport of that specific deployment strategy configuration (maxSurge: 0, maxUnavailable: 1) is requested for the v0.11 branch to unblock EUS upgrade paths (4.18 -> 4.20) for GitOps/ZTP customers.{noformat}

In environments with small footprints (such as clusters with exactly 2 schedulable worker nodes), the existing v0.10.2 pods occupy 100% of the available scheduling slots. 
Consequently, the new v0.11.0 pods cannot satisfy the anti-affinity/spread constraints and remain permanently in a 'Pending' state. This triggers an OLM installation timeout after exceeding the progress deadline.

Proof & Log Evidence
The scheduler explicitly drops the pods with the following constraint message:
0/8 nodes are available: 2 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master: }, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node.ocs.openshift.io/storage: true}.

A side-by-side verification confirms that SNR v0.10.2 did not enforce this constraint, while v0.11.0 introduces it as a hard rule, breaking the upgrade path for 2-node worker topologies. 

Requested Action / Fix
Please backport the deployment rollout strategy fix already present in SNR v0.12 (upstream main branch) into the v0.11 stream. The fix enforces:
* maxSurge: 0
* maxUnavailable: 1

This layout forces a "one-out, one-in" eviction flow that clears a node slot *before* attempting to schedule the new replica, resolving the deadlock.problem here>{noformat}

*Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):*

{noformat}self-node-remediation-operator v0.11.0 (on RHOCP 4.20.14){noformat}

*How reproducible:*

{noformat}Always (100% reproducible on clusters with exactly 2 schedulable worker nodes during the upgrade path from v0.10.2).{noformat}

*Steps to Reproduce:*

{noformat}1. Deploy Self Node Remediation (SNR) operator version v0.10.2 on an OpenShift cluster with only 2 schedulable worker nodes (e.g., 3 Masters, 3 Storage, 2 Workers topology).
2. Trigger a cluster upgrade or operator subscription upgrade to target SNR v0.11.0.
3. Observe the OLM installation phase and check the scheduling status of the new controller-manager pods.{noformat}

*Actual results:*

{noformat}The upgrade process hangs and eventually times out into an 'InstallCheckFailed' state. The new SNR v0.11.0 manager pods remain indefinitely in a 'Pending' state due to unsatisfied topology spread constraints, as the legacy v0.10.2 pods continue to occupy the only 2 available worker nodes.{noformat}

*Expected results:*

{noformat}The operator upgrade rollout should execute smoothly without blocking itself. The deployment strategy should clean up/evict old replicas sequentially (e.g., via maxSurge: 0 / maxUnavailable: 1) to free up node space before trying to schedule the newer v0.11.0 replicas on small-footprint environments.{noformat}

*Additional info:*

{noformat}The issue has already been resolved in upstream version SNR v0.12 by adjusting the rollout strategy requirements. 
A backport of that specific deployment strategy configuration (maxSurge: 0, maxUnavailable: 1) is requested for the v0.11 branch to unblock EUS upgrade paths (4.18 -> 4.20) for GitOps/ZTP customers.{noformat}

items.toString: This work item links to "medik8s/storage-based-remediation#59: Align CI workflows with standard medik8s pattern (Web Link)"

h3. Context

SBR uses non-standard GitHub Actions workflows ({{test.yml}}, {{build-images.yml}}, {{build-dev-images.yml}}) that diverge from the established medik8s pattern used by FAR, SNR, NHC, MDR, and NMO ({{pre-submit.yaml}}, {{post-submit.yaml}}, {{release.yaml}}). This creates maintenance overhead and prevents reuse of shared tooling.

h3. Current issues

* {{build-dev-images.yml}} is broken — Quay.io push fails with unauthorized (see [PR #58 CI failure|https://github.com/medik8s/storage-based-remediation/actions/runs/26402841516/job/77721702705])
* No {{release.yaml}} — SBR cannot do automated OLM releases or community operator PRs
* No bundle/manifest verification in pre-submit ({{verify-bundle}}, {{verify-vendor}})
* No container build in pre-submit (others run {{make container-build-community}})
* Shallow clone ({{fetch-depth: 1}}) breaks version detection tooling
* Triggers on all branches instead of {{main}} + {{release-*}} only
* {{.yml}} extension instead of standard {{.yaml}}

h3. Proposed changes

* Replace {{test.yml}} with standard {{pre-submit.yaml}} (trigger on main/release-*, fetch-depth: 0, add {{make container-build-community}}, add bundle verification)
* Replace {{build-images.yml}} with standard {{post-submit.yaml}} (single-arch {{make container-build-and-push-community}}, push to main only)
* Add {{release.yaml}} following FAR/SNR pattern (workflow_dispatch, versioned images, GitHub Release, community operator PRs via {{medik8s/.github}} reusable workflow)
* Remove {{build-dev-images.yml}} (broken, redundant with pre-submit)

h3. Reference

* FAR workflows: [pre-submit|https://github.com/medik8s/fence-agents-remediation/blob/main/.github/workflows/pre-submit.yaml], [post-submit|https://github.com/medik8s/fence-agents-remediation/blob/main/.github/workflows/post-submit.yaml], [release|https://github.com/medik8s/fence-agents-remediation/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml]
* SBR current: [workflows|https://github.com/medik8s/storage-based-remediation/tree/main/.github/workflows]

items.fromString:
Create a new architecture image in Konflux for SBR for ARM (*arm64*), following [multi-arch design doc|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uW8F8E_o-3NweFx0knMOuj8GWGf40H9NfSYjWEUEDEY/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.ncf37fq99jag].

Following [Konflux multi-platform builds|https://konflux.pages.redhat.com/docs/users/getting-started/multi-platform-builds.html], this new architecture is supported by Konflux.

For more, read at [Konflux onboarding docs|https://github.com/konflux-ci/olm-operator-konflux-sample/blob/e0fe58178ff82586cfd004065d0586f016aa6a9a/docs/konflux-onboarding.md#customize-tekton-pipleines]

See an example at [rh-kmm-konflux2|https://github.com/chr15p/rh-kmm-konflux2]

*Actions*:

* Provide support for SBR operator and agent images in the new architecture (amd64/arm64/ppc64le/s390x)
* Use [different build recipe per architecture|https://konflux.pages.redhat.com/docs/users/getting-started/multi-platform-builds.html#different-build-recipe-per-architecture] for a distinctive Go build binary until upstream code has been changed [hack/build.sh|https://github.com/medik8s/storage-based-remediation/blob/main/hack/build.sh]
* Provide support for SBR bundle image on multiple architectures (amd64/arm64/ppc64le/s390x) by adding new labels to bundle's CSV - [multi-arch docs|https://sdk.operatorframework.io/docs/advanced-topics/multi-arch/]
